newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IBM plans China venture fund injection.
newsitem.headline: IBM plans China venture fund injection.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp (IBM) plans to boost investment in its biggest China venture, Shenzhen Hailiang Storage Product Co Ltd, an IBM official said on Thursday.
"The plan is still in a preliminary stage," the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
"We probably will increase our investment in the venture because it has a bright future," said the official at IBM China-H.K. Corp, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the U.S.-based computer giant.
She said the size of the injetion is not yet known, but a Hailiang official said IBM planned to invest at least $40 million.
If IBM decides to boost its investment, it would require the final approval of China's ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation, the IBM official said.
Hailiang, with a total investment of US$42.5 million, on Tuesday began making computer hard drive components for IBM's plants across the world, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said on Wednesday.
IBM has an 80 percent stake in Hailiang, which was set up in Shenzhen with registered capital of US$20 million, a Hailiang official said on Wednesday.
The remaining 20 percent interest is evenly split between Shenzhen Kaifa Technology Co Ltd, a listed computer parts maker, and the China Great Wall Computer Co, the Hailiang official said.
With four production lines from Japan, the venture expects to produce 36 million components worth US$250 million in 1997, the Hailiang official said.
